To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the A6 clone is a useful model for the study of sodium transport, but is not suitable for the study of chloride transport.
the A6 cell line is not an appropriate model to study the effects of aldosterone in the distal renal nephron.
the effects of aldosterone were studied by electrophysiological measurements in A6 monalayers and in amphibian skin epithelia (ASE).
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the analysis of the mechanisms underlying the effects of aldosterone.
the role of epithelial structure in the response to aldosterone.
the role of aldosterone in sodium transport, and more particularly with the role of chloride permeability in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chloride conductance of the A6 cell line is not aldosterone-dependent and that the conductive chloride pathway in the A6 cell is not a prerequisite for aldosterone-dependent sodium reabsorption.
the aldosterone-induced chloride conductance pathway is a specific feature of the distal nephron.

, in A6 cells, aldosterone increases sodium transport by increasing the conductive component of the apical sodium entry pathway and by decreasing the conductive component in the paracellular pathway, while the chloride pathway remains unchanged.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aldosterone stimulates sodium transport in A6 cells by increasing the activity of the sodium pump and the conductive chloride pathway in the basolateral membrane.
the aldosterone-induced increase in sodium transport in A6 cell monolaers is associated with an increase in cell conductance, but not shunt conductance.
aldosterone is a key regulator of sodium transport in A6 monolyayers, but it does not induce a chloride conductive pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the aldosterone-induced chloride reabsorption in distal tubules and collecting ducts of the mammalian kidney is not a universal phenomenon.
the presence of a conductive chloride pathway in aldosteroneresponsive, Na+ transporting epithelia is dependent on the presence of a heterogeneous epithelium.
A6 monolayer and ASE are two structurally and functionally distinct epithelial models, which can be used to study the effects of hormones, including aldosterone, on ion transport.
